pr.title: Add Tabs group interface
pr.body: ## Scope Adds Tabs group interface as a really nice alternative to accordion interface. Works 100% with collaborative editing. **What's changed:** - Migrates the community directus-extension-group-tabs-interface (from your boi @hanneskuettner) into Directus core as a new group-tabs interface - Built on reka-ui Tabs components (already a dependency) — gives us WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, roving tabindex, keyboard nav (arrows, Home/End), and RTL support for free - Adds fillWidth option to allow the tab group to span the full page width - Fixes several bugs from the original extension: validation error auto-switch was using the wrong array index, hidden first tab caused a blank panel, and RTL keyboard nav didn't work - Validation error tooltips show all errors per tab with field names (matching group-detail pattern) instead of just the first error - Full feature parity with other group interfaces: ComparisonContext support for revision diff indicators, CollabContext passthrough, nonEditable prop, logical CSS properties for RTL ## Potential Risks / Drawbacks - No existing tests for any group interface (accordion, detail, raw) so no test coverage added here either — consistent with current state but worth flagging - fillWidth is a new option unique to group-tabs — no other group interface has it yet (but it is valuable) ## Tested Scenarios - Tab switching, keyboard nav (ArrowLeft/Right, Home/End) - Edit dot indicators showing on tabs with unsaved changes - Validation errors: auto-switches to the correct tab including for nested field errors, tooltip shows all errors - Hidden tabs filtered correctly — no blank panels - fillWidth option spans the full grid width - Collab editing context passes through to nested VForm ## Review Notes / Questions - Used reka-ui Tabs instead of hand-rolling tab logic — seemed like a no-brainer since we already use reka-ui for Accordion, Collapsible, and DatePicker in core - The useComputedGroup() pattern is identical to group-accordion.vue — could potentially be extracted into a shared composable later but kept inline for now to match existing conventions - Edit dot is positioned inline (left of field name) rather than absolutely positioned outside the trigger like accordion does — absolute positioning caused the dot to bleed into the gap between tabs ## Checklist - ~~Added or updated tests~~ - [Documentation PR created here or not required](https://github.com/directus/docs/pull/584) - ~~OpenAPI package PR created here or not required~~

review_comments.body: When I have the extension installed, I cannot select Tabs or Group Tabs as an interface by itself. If I select one, the other one comes along for the ride. This continues to happen even after uninstalling the extension. I think this interface id is the same one used by the extension, so maybe by changing it here, we can avoid this double selection behavior.

in props, this is typed as <string, unknown> so I suggest using that same type here for consistency. It should be inferred, so you can just leave the type off here altogether.

```suggestion
	const groupValues = ref(props.values);
```

Even _after_ uninstalling the extension? That seems like a weird one to me. Could you double check if your client bundle updated? The extension information should not be available anymore after uninstalling.
@hanneskuettner you're right. I had to re-run the build after uninstalling the extension.
Huh that also seems weird, tbh. Reloading the page should be enough as the `extensions` bundle should be regenerated at that point
We can change the ID if needed but was just trying to make the process as seamless as possible.

@bryantgillespie that's probably fine, it just might be a bit odd for user that already have the extension installed, and experience both interfaces being selected any time they add or remove on of the tabs interfaces. Not a huge deal though, so I'm fine with whatever you think is best here.

@@ -0,0 +1,36 @@
+import { defineInterface } from '@directus/extensions';
+import InterfaceGroupTabs from './group-tabs.vue';
+import PreviewSVG from './preview.svg?raw';
+
+export default defineInterface({
+	id: 'group-tabs',
+	name: '$t:interfaces.group-tabs.name',
+	description: '$t:interfaces.group-tabs.description',
+	icon: 'tab',
+	component: InterfaceGroupTabs,
+	hideLabel: true,
+	hideLoader: true,
+	autoKey: true,
+	types: ['alias'],
+	localTypes: ['group'],
+	group: 'group',
+	options: [
+		{
+			field: 'fillWidth',
+			type: 'boolean',
+			name: '$t:interfaces.group-tabs.overwrite_group_width',
+			meta: {
+				interface: 'boolean',
+				note: '$t:interfaces.group-tabs.fill_width_note',
+				options: {
+					label: '$t:interfaces.group-tabs.fill_width',
+				},
+				width: 'half',
+			},
+			schema: {
+				default_value: false,
+			},
+		},
+	],
+	preview: PreviewSVG,
+});
